newsitem.title: USA: Memtec says to proceed with Gelman deal.
newsitem.headline: Memtec says to proceed with Gelman deal.

text.p: Memtec Ltd said it plans to proceed with its proposed $280-million stock acquisition of Gelman Sciences Inc, despite the news that Gelman is in talks with Pall Corp about a possible deal.

"We're continuing to proceed under the agreement to acquire Gelman. That is our intention," said Kevin O'Neill, general counsel for Memtec America, the U.S. unit of Australia's Memtec, in an interview with Reuters.
O'Neill declined further comment, but confirmed that Memtec issued a statement on Thursday morning saying that it has been advised by Gelman of its discussions with Pall.
A Pall spokeswoman said the company planned to issue a statement on Thursday. Gelman executives could not be reached.
In the statement from Australian headquarters, Memtec said it was advised by Gelman that "Gelman Sciences Inc received an inquiry from Pall Corporation with respect to an acquisition transaction."

Pall has not made an offer, but Gelman "has determined to engage in discussions regarding Pall's inquiry and to furnish certain information to Pall regarding the company, its business, properties and assets," the statement said.
"This information will be provided during discussions which are scheduled to begin Thursday, Oct. 10.," the statement said.
Trading in shares in Ann Arbor, Mich.-based Gelman was halted for an imbalance early Thursday on the American Stock Exchange. Shares in Pall, based in East Hills, N.Y., were off 3/8 to 26-1/4.

In its statement, Memtec said that Gelman cited a clause in their merger agreement that would allow Gelman to terminate the agreement "if Gelman determines that the acquisition transaction (with Pall) is more favorable from a financial point of view than the merger with Memtec and the directors of Gelman determine that it is necessary to do so to act consistently with their fiduciary obligations."

Gelman makes microfiltration products for laboratories, healthcare, environmental monitoring, high-technology process industries and other uses. Memtec is also in the purification and separation business.

The two signed a definitive merger agreement in late August in which Memtec agreed to exchange 1.05 Memtec American depository shares for each share of Gelman. The deal is collared so that Gelman may call it off or renegotiate if the Memtec ADSs trade at an average price of less than $30 each over the 45-day period preceding the closing date.
Pall is also in the purification and filtration business, with emphasis on the healthcare, aerospace and fluid processing markets.

When Memtec first bid for Gelman in July, analysts said Pall might be among rival bidders, although they considered a competing offer unlikely. Others named by analysts as possibly interested in Gelman were Millipore Corp and Osmonics Inc.
